project: TheosophicalAlchemyDB - Maier Atalanta Fugiens Emblem Extraction
scholarship: Helena Maria Elisabeth De Jong, Michael Maier's Atalanta Fugiens: Sources of an Alchemical Book of Emblems (Nicolas-Hays, Inc., 2002)
methodology: Visual description (objective), Philosophical meaning (De Jong interpretation), Key concepts (alchemical framework), Related concepts (thematic connections), De Jong citations (scholarly attribution)

emblems.title: Put a toad to the breasts of a woman, that she may feed it, and the woman may die

emblems.title: Send your son and daughter into the bath, that with their skin changed they come out white

emblems.title: Do not separate the subtle from the gross in the beginning

emblems.title: Putrefaction is the beginning of generation

emblems.title: Hide the hermaphrodite from the rays of the sun, that it may be nourished in darkness

emblems.spiritual_meaning: The hidden inner light, divine knowledge concealed from the profane

emblems.title: Make the stone equal in weight to its humidity

emblems.spiritual_meaning: The burning away of impurities, contemplative fire of the soul

gender_awareness_notes: Emblems II, III, V, VI, XXXV (not included here) emphasize women's work and knowledge. Maier credits women's practical knowledge of laundering, cooking, nursing, and textile dyeing as sources of alchemical understanding. The feminine principle (Earth, Water, the receptive force) is essential to the work, never subordinate. De Jong emphasizes that Maier's move to include domestic labor as a teaching source was radical for his time.
rosicrucian_resonance: Throughout these twenty emblems, Maier's Rosicrucian ideals appear: the defense of legitimate hermetic wisdom against fraud, the emphasis on secrecy and sacred knowledge for the initiated only, the equation of the Fraternity's goals with the ancient alchemical tradition (Hermes Trismegistus, Raymond Lullius), the transformation of the soul through knowledge of nature's secrets, the ideal of the wise sage or perfected individual.
